stories.headline: PSD withdraws from Bolojan coalition government, ministers resign, no-confidence motion threatened
stories.summary: Romania's largest party, PSD, voted to withdraw political support for Liberal PM Ilie Bolojan on April 20, and seven ministers formally resigned on April 23, stripping the coalition of its parliamentary majority. President Nicușor Dan signed the resignations on April 25 and convened cross-party consultations for April 28, while Bolojan refused to step down and PSD prepared a no-confidence motion; ratings agencies and BNR warned of economic consequences and EU funds access risk.

stories.headline: Russian drone debris falls on Romanian territory; RAF Typhoons scrambled from Romanian air base
stories.summary: During a massive Russian overnight drone attack on Ukraine on April 25, fragments from two Russian drones landed in the Romanian city of Galați and Tulcea county, damaging property and prompting evacuations of roughly 200 people; Romania's foreign ministry summoned the Russian ambassador and the president called it the first incident where Romanian property was actually damaged. Two RAF Eurofighter Typhoons deployed at Romania's Borcea air base were scrambled and authorized to engage aerial targets, though the UK later clarified no drones were shot down; Romania also announced tests of an AI-powered US-made drone interceptor system at Capu Midia days earlier.

stories.headline: George Simion uses disability slur against President Dan, faces anti-discrimination complaint and internal AUR rebuke
stories.summary: AUR leader George Simion called President Nicușor Dan a 'paraplegic' in a public speech in Târgu Mureș on April 23, provoking USR to file a formal complaint with the National Anti-Discrimination Council (CNCD), which opened an investigation; Simion continued his attacks and AUR co-founder Marius Lulea publicly disavowed the language, calling it behavior of a 'spoiled child.' The incident coincided with Simion announcing AUR would file its own no-confidence motion against the Bolojan government in May.

stories.headline: Romania tests US-made AI-powered drone interceptors at Black Sea base; army plans €400M drone investment
stories.summary: Reuters reported on April 24 that Romania conducted final tests of Merops AI-powered drone interceptors made by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt's Project Eagle at the Capu Midia base overlooking the Black Sea, with the system to be deployed within days. Separately, the Romanian Army announced plans to invest over €400 million in drone systems in coming years, and Defence Minister Radu Miruță invited participating companies to join real operations alongside Romanian soldiers.

stories.headline: Marcel Ciolacu linked to luxury Herăstrău penthouse amid allegations of opaque property connections
stories.summary: G4Media reported that former PM and current Buzău County Council President Marcel Ciolacu is allegedly renting a 350 sqm penthouse in the upscale One Herăstrău complex in Bucharest, where he reportedly lives with companion Sorina Docuz; the property was purchased in September 2025 for €8.13 million by a Buzău-registered firm linked to an obscure American company with non-public shareholders and which had previously sold advertising for PSD. Ciolacu denied the allegations, but multiple outlets identified additional financial and political connections surrounding the acquisition.

stories.headline: BNR intervenes to defend leu, warns of economic consequences as political crisis deepens
stories.summary: Romania's National Bank (BNR) sold over €1 billion from its reserves in March to defend the leu and continued interventions in April amid the political crisis; a BNR governor's adviser publicly warned that PSD 'could hardly have chosen a worse moment' for the coalition rupture, highlighting risks to the PNRR funds and credit rating. BNR also kept its policy rate unchanged at 6.50% for the 13th consecutive session and flagged elevated exchange rate risks in its April board minutes.
